Hi team, could I get some <#C081MV728N7>  with a data type replication issue?

We have an `INT` column in our MariaDB source, and we expect it to be replicated as `INT` in the destination Parquet files on S3. However, OLake is consistently writing the column as `BIGINT`/`INT64` in the Parquet schema.

*Source:* MariaDB (MySQL) — `INT(11)`
*Destination:* S3 — Parquet

We were initially running OLake *v0.6.4*, and I suspected this might be version-specific. I also tested the same table with *v0.10.0*, but the column is still being written as `BIGINT`/`INT64`.

This isn't blocking us immediately, but we'd like to understand the root cause before proceeding further, especially since the expected source-to-destination data type mapping is important for our downstream analytical workloads.

Could someone please help us understand why `INT(11)` is being mapped to `BIGINT`/`INT64` in the Parquet output? Is there any configuration or recommended approach to preserve the `INT` data type?

Any guidance or pointers to the relevant code/documentation would be greatly appreciated. Thanks!

text:
`INT UNSIGNED` used to map to 32-bit, which overflowed above 2,147,483,647. We fixed it in *v0.4.1* (<https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/846|PR #846>) so it now maps to 64-bit.
The fix is behind a state-version check so existing jobs don't change type mid-sync: your older table keeps `INT32`, while any newly created job gets the corrected `BIGINT`.
